reality_delta: Main AI frames this as a simple calibration error (45s < 59s → raise the number), but skips the harder questions: why did the check grow to 59s, is it still growing, and what margin methodology prevents this from recurring as enforcement rules accumulate? The proposed fix treats the symptom without adding the guardrail that would make the next exhaustion event diagnosable before an E2E run fails. A check that takes 59 seconds is one incremental rule away from failing again — the fix needs a margin methodology, not just a bigger number.
main_concern: No specific target timeout value is proposed, and no margin methodology is stated. The main AI says "raise to a calibrated value above observed full-check duration" but never names the value or formula. Without a concrete number, the fix cannot be reviewed: is it 65s (10% margin, will re-fail soon), 90s (50%), or 120s (2x, masks hangs)? A "calibrated value" without a number is a placeholder the main AI can fill with whatever feels right at implementation time, defeating the purpose of a pre-implementation review.
top_risks: Underspecified calibration target — no concrete timeout value or margin formula, so fix is indistinguishable from 'pick a bigger number.' Future enforcement-rules will grow and exhaust any picked number; without a margin methodology, this failure mode recurs silently.

Child/outer timeout race condition — the request asks about child/outer relationship but the main claim doesn't address it. If outer=120s and child=90s, a 95s run exhausts outer before child fires, producing confusing failure modes that are less diagnosable than the current 45s timeout signal.

Self-check mechanism is entirely undefined — 'add self-check coverage' could mean a 60s integration test that makes CI unusable, or a static assertion fragile to environment changes. The mechanism matters enormously for both effectiveness and development velocity.
missing_evidence: Timeout variance data — only single-point measurements (59.215s, 63.248s) cited. No min/max/stddev across multiple runs/environments. Single warm-run measurement insufficient for calibration.
Current outer timeout value — the outer timeout is referenced as a constraint but its actual configuration is never stated. Cannot size child budget without knowing outer budget.
Enforcement-check duration trend — was 59s always the duration or has it been growing? At what rate? Without trend data, any picked number guesses about unobserved future behavior.
minimum_fix: 1. State the exact new timeout value with margin formula (minimum: max(observed_max × 1.5, observed_max + 30s)) documented with measurement date. 2. Define child/outer timeout relationship with a startup assertion (e.g., outer ≥ child + 30s). 3. Specify the concrete self-check mechanism — not a hand-wave. 4. Collect ≥3 runs of variance data in the target E2E environment before setting the final number.

anti_loop_signal.reason: Main AI correctly identifies this as third E2E attempt, rejects 'bypass or weaken' in favor of recalibration, showing loop awareness. However, the risk of a new silent-drift loop (raise timeout, enforcement grows, raise again) is unaddressed. No early-warning guardrail proposed that would detect the next imminent timeout exhaustion before an E2E run fails.
